text:
The bloodless Man, through flowering meadows,

walks, dressed in black, cigar in mouth;

the bloodless Man evokes Tuileries in bloom,

—and his dead eye sometimes takes on gleams of fire...


Drunk, the Emperor, after twenty years of orgy,

thought: "I will blow on Liberty

very carefully, as on a candle!"

Liberty is reborn!... —and he is broken-backed!


He is imprisoned. —What name on his echoless lips

throbs? what implacable longing bites him?

No one will know, for Caesar has the dead eye.


Perhaps he thinks of his little-bespectacled Crony...

—And look how from his lit cigar flows,

as in Saint-Cloud, at night, the tenuous blue cloud.

translation.title: Rages of Caesars
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the satirical imperial portrait, dead eye, and cigar-smoke memory.
